correctness.rationale: For p>=5, the indicator expansion has q empty contribution, zero singleton contributions, six pair sums exactly -1 each, at most four cubic sums of magnitude 2sqrt(q), and one monic smooth quartic sum at least -2sqrt(q)-1 from genus-one Hasse with two rational infinity points. The four excluded starts contribute at most 32, giving 16N>=q-10sqrt(q)-39=(sqrt(q)-13)(sqrt(q)+3), strictly positive for q>169. The deterministic finite certificate exhausts all 42 prime powers q<=169 of characteristic>=5, uses certified irreducible polynomial fields and Euler-character cross-checks, and yields exactly the stated 13 exceptions. For characteristic 3, the first and fourth shifts coincide; in characteristic 2 all nonzero elements are squares. Boundaries q=169 and q=53 are explicitly covered.

value.rationale: The full 16-word universality property is a canonical finite-field character-pattern existence invariant, relevant to questions about quadratic-residue strings. The exact exceptional-order list, sharp 59 cutoff and extension-field failures at 25 and 49 distinguish least successful order 37 from eventual uniform success; they settle a natural all-prime-power variant not covered by prime-only formulas. The infinite tail is established analytically and the finite part is completely certified, not a sampled census. No new complexity/security theorem or broad counting theory is asserted.
